title: Fusus al-Hikam
author: ibn-arabi
attributionNote: The attribution to Ibn Arabi is the one the manuscript tradition gives; the work's teachings, not its authorship, were the subject of later dispute.
description: Twenty-seven chapters, each built around a prophet or a figure of the Qur'an, in which Ibn Arabi reads the stories as aspects of the relation between the one reality and the many forms in which it appears. The book is dense with scriptural allusion and became the focus of centuries of commentary and dispute.
historicalContext: Written late in Ibn Arabi's life, after his move to Damascus. Its teaching on the unity of being was defended and attacked by later scholars, and the work was commented on by authors from al-Qashani to al-Jandi. The attribution to Ibn Arabi is the one the manuscript tradition gives.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
